Part 1 · ESG and the double materiality assessment

Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD)

The CSRD is the legal basis that asks many companies to give clear information about how they protect the environment, how they treat people, and how they are managed. The goal is to help the public and investors understand how sustainable a company is.

Update 2026

In 2026, the EU simplified the CSRD (“Omnibus I”, in force since 18 March 2026). Since then, the obligation to report only applies to very large companies: companies with more than 1,000 employees and a net turnover of more than €450 million. The ESRS will also be simplified.

European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS)

European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) are a framework for the preparation of sustainability reports. The aim of the ESRS is to provide uniform regulations for corporate reporting on ESG issues.

IBV 11 · Case study LEGO GroupESG and the double materiality assessment
Part 1 · ESG and the double materiality assessment

E … S … G

The term “ESG” stands for Environmental, Social and Governance, …

EEnvironmental

What impact does a company have on the environment, and what opportunities and risks result from environmental issues for the company´s financial situation?
⬇

ESG-related standards (ESRS)

SSocial

What impact does a company have on social issues, and what opportunities and risks result from social matters for the company´s financial situation?
⬇

ESG-related standards (ESRS)

GGovernance

What impact does a company have on business relationships or corporate culture, and what opportunities and risks result from this for the company´s financial situation?
⬇

ESG-related standards (ESRS)

IBV 11 · Case study LEGO GroupESG and the double materiality assessment
Part 1 · ESG and the double materiality assessment

Which ESG topics are material for the company? – The double materiality assessment

Step 1 · Identify ESG matters and related ESRS …

… with the help of the double materiality assessment. This always includes two perspectives.

Step 2 · The two perspectives: inside-out and outside-in

Step 3 · When does the company have to report?

Information must be reported if it is material from one of the two perspectives.

Step 4 · Which part of the business?

upstream(e. g. suppliers)
The assessment considers the company´s entire value chain
downstream(e. g. customers)
End of part 1

Go back to your script. In the next part you see how a real company – Adidas AG – carries out the double materiality assessment.

The double materiality assessment – Adidas AG as an example

Topical ESRS / Topic / Sub-topic / Sub-sub-topicMaterial ImpactsDescription
EEnvironmental (ESRS E1) / Climate Change / EnergyNegative impactAdidas has a multi-stage supply chain with energy-intensive raw material production and manufacturing processes that still partially rely on non-renewable energy sources leading to Green House Gas emissions.
SSocial (ESRS S1) / Own workforce / working conditions / Adequate wagesPositive impactProviding flexible and fair working time and rules for employees actively supports employee well-being and work-life balance.
GGovernance (ESRS G1) / Business conduct / Protection of whistle blowersNegative impactEven with elaborate whistleblower protection in place, there can still be negative personal impacts if these measures fail in certain cases.

Source: report.adidas-group.com/2024/en/group-management-report-sustainability-statement/esrs-2-general-disclosures/overview.html. Accessed on 30 June 2025.
